page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is a shared-core virtual server built on x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 2 vCPUs powered by a single physical Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 40 MB of L3 cache, with instruction support for AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2. The instance contains no local disk storage and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth specification.

Performance benchmarks reflect the constrained nature of the shared CPU environment. In synthetic compute evaluations, stress-ng yields 945.88 for single-core and 1857.99 for multi-core performance, placing it in low comparative percentiles. PassMark CPU testing logs a total score of 2538.35 with an extended instructions rating of 1978.53. Memory throughput measures 164.27 GB/sec for small cached blocks, declining to 14.95 GB/sec for uncached reads and 11.46 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application-level tests demonstrate 2.53 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 2.31 GB/sec.

The configuration delivers high memory density relative to compute resources, prioritizing cost efficiency for workloads with low CPU utilization demands. The lack of dedicated CPU allocation and local disk storage presents a trade-off, restricting execution speeds during sustained parallel tasks. Recommended workload fits include non-production staging environments, small-scale caching layers, internal utility tools, and low-traffic web serving where memory availability takes precedence over processor throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an entry-level virtual server instance driven by a shared Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 2 vCPUs across a single physical core with hyperthreading and KVM virtualization, it provides 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware features 40 MB of L3 cache, basic AVX instruction support, no bundled local storage, and zero baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in low performance tiers across compute and memory metrics, recording a stress-ng single-core score of 945.88 and uncached memory write speed of 11.46 GB/sec. Application tests show modest output, such as 2.53 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.31 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Designed with cost efficiency for memory-heavy, compute-light requirements, ecs.e4.large is best suited for non-production environments, staging servers, lightweight caching layers, or low-throughput internal web applications.
